title: A link is an untrusted input
summary: Review an open deep link, choose tests for host and route boundaries, and map links to authenticated routes.

scenario.briefing: The campus app registers a custom scheme and accepts any URL. The handler reads a redirect parameter and sends the user to it after login. A phishing link used the app to bounce users to a look-alike site. Review the configuration before adding universal links.

objectives.description: Identify open-host, open-redirect, and unauthenticated link risks.
Choose tests for host, route, and session boundaries.
Explain verified links, allowlists, and route mapping.

hints: A custom scheme can be registered by any app.
The host and path both need validation.
A redirect parameter is an open redirect unless it is constrained.
Map known hosts and routes to app screens; require a session for private screens.

misconceptions.description: Treating a custom URL scheme as proof of the sender.
misconceptions.feedback: Any app can register or send a custom scheme. Use verified universal or app links and validate the host and route.

misconceptions.description: Testing only the link the app itself generates.
misconceptions.feedback: An attacker does not use your generated link. Test foreign hosts, encoded paths, and unauthenticated access.

misconceptions.description: Checking the scheme but not the host or path.
misconceptions.feedback: A valid scheme can carry any host and path. Validate both against an allowlist before routing.

sections.title: Links arrive from anywhere
sections.body: A deep link is an input from the operating system, a browser, or another app. The sender is not authenticated. Custom schemes are easy to imitate, and encoded paths can hide traversal or extra segments.

sections.title: Verified links and allowlists
sections.body: Universal links (iOS) and app links (Android) verify that the app controls the domain. Even then, route only known hosts and paths. Map a path to an internal screen; never redirect to a raw URL from the link.

sections.title: Session belongs in the route
sections.body: A link to an order or message screen must require the same session check as the in-app navigation. A link is not proof of identity, and it must not bypass authentication.

vocabulary.definition: A URL that opens a specific screen or resource in an app.
An iOS link verified against a domain the app controls.
An Android link verified with a digital asset association.
A redirect that accepts an attacker-controlled destination.

findings.label: The app accepts links from any host.
The redirect parameter sends the user to an unvalidated URL.
The order route is opened without checking the session.
The raw id parameter is concatenated into a route.
A custom scheme identifies the sending app.

verdicts.label: Block until hosts, routes, redirects, and sessions are constrained

steps.explanation: The app trusts any host and redirects to a raw URL. The order route also needs a session check and a validated id.

steps.title: Choose the link tests
steps.prompt: Select the tests you would keep for the handler.
hints: Start with the valid campus link.
Add a foreign host and a different scheme.
Add an encoded path and an unauthenticated private route.
Keep valid, foreign host, wrong scheme, encoded path, and no-session cases; drop the self-generated duplicate.

cases.label: https://campus.test/order?id=17 opens the signed-in order → accepted
Valid order link without a session → login, then the order
The link the app generated itself → accepted

steps.explanation: Link tests must include foreign hosts, wrong schemes, encoded paths, and unauthenticated private routes. Testing only your own link proves little.

steps.title: Route links deliberately
hints: The scheme alone does not identify the sender.
Map paths to screens instead of redirecting raw URLs.
Private screens need the same session check as in-app navigation.
Select verified links, host and path allowlists, mapped routes, and session checks; reject scheme-only trust.

statements.label: Universal and app links verify that the app controls the linked domain.
The handler should allow only known hosts and paths.
A path should map to an internal screen, not to a raw redirect destination.
Private screens reached by a link still require a session check.
Checking the URL scheme is enough because another app cannot use it.

steps.explanation: Link safety comes from verified domains, allowlisted paths, mapped routes, and the same authorization checks as in-app navigation.
